name: ai-reviewed-challenge-v1-disagreements
comparisonPolicy: Compare roots, POS and segmentation alternatives as unordered sets. Each segmentation retains its ordered spans and exact type/start/end. Omitted expectedError equals false. Ordering-only differences, confidence and prose differences are not substantive field disagreements; full original records are preserved for every substantive disagreement.

originalA.notes: Reader or reading active participle; also the regular Form III imperative قَارِئْ from قارأ, inferred from the dictionary lemma. Bare ء represents the hamza radical.

originalB.notes: Reader/reading active participle. The radical hamza is written bare in the root.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain verb: the Academy attests Form III قارأ; قَارِئْ is its regular imperative, inferred by conjugation. B omitted this supported homograph.

final.notes: Reader or reading active participle; also the regular Form III imperative قَارِئْ from قارأ, inferred from the dictionary lemma. Bare ء represents the hamza radical.

originalA.notes: Reading, a verbal noun. Terminal ة may remain part of its lexical stem or be represented as a derivational ending; it is not a separate feminine agreement suffix here.

originalB.notes: Reading/recitation verbal noun; final ة may be kept within the lexical stem or separated under the contract's unspecified feminine convention.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose A. قراءة is a verbal noun; retain lexical-whole and derivational ة analyses. Reject B's inflectional_suffix variant because lexical femininity alone does not establish productive gender agreement.

final.notes: Reading, a verbal noun. Terminal ة may remain part of its lexical stem or be represented as a derivational ending; it is not a separate feminine agreement suffix here.

originalA.notes: سَائِل is asker/beggar from سءل or fluid/flowing from سيل. Verb accepts the Form III imperative سَائِلْ from ساءل; the perfect سَاءَلَ has different spelling.

originalB.notes: Questioner/beggar from سأل; flowing or a liquid from سال يسيل. These homographs have distinct roots.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain verb: the Academy attests ساءل, whose regular imperative is سَائِلْ. The verb alternative has root سءل; flowing/liquid has root سيل.

final.notes: سَائِل is asker/beggar from سءل or fluid/flowing from سيل. Verb accepts the Form III imperative سَائِلْ from ساءل; the perfect سَاءَلَ has different spelling.

originalA.notes: Indefinite defective active participle دَاعٍ, caller/cause; final radical و has no separate surface span. Also the regular imperative دَاعِ from dictionary-attested داعى, inferred by conjugation.

originalB.notes: Caller/inviter, or a motive/cause; indefinite defective participle داعٍ with the final ي absent in this spelling.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain verb: the Academy attests داعى. Its regular masculine singular imperative دَاعِ omits the final weak letter, yielding داع. This is a conjugational inference.

final.notes: Indefinite defective active participle دَاعٍ, caller/cause; final radical و has no separate surface span. Also the regular imperative دَاعِ from dictionary-attested داعى, inferred by conjugation.

originalA.notes: رَامٍ is a thrower/archer from رمي; رَامَ sought/desired is from روم; رَامَ departed or a wound healed is from ريم. The last is less common and dictionary-attested. Imperative رَامِ from رامى also has root رمي.

originalB.notes: Archer/throwing (raamin) from رمى; sought/attempted (raama) from رام يروم. Lane also records a tree noun رام under روم. Foreign name/acronym readings are outside this set.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain ريم in addition to رمي and روم: the Academy directly lists رام for departing or a wound closing under ريم. This is a distinct lexical homograph.

final.notes: رَامٍ is a thrower/archer from رمي; رَامَ sought/desired is from روم; رَامَ departed or a wound healed is from ريم. The last is less common and dictionary-attested. Imperative رَامِ from رامى also has root رمي.

originalA.notes: Strong/severe/intense; root has repeated د radicals.

originalB.notes: Strong/severe; noun is accepted for a substantivized strong/severe person or thing. Radical د is doubled.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose adjective. B supplies generic substantivization but no distinct conventional noun sense; do not automatically add noun to every adjective for an ellipted referent.

final.notes: Strong/severe/intense adjective, root شدد. Generic noun-like use after ellipsis is not enough here to add a separate noun POS; this noun/adjective boundary remains a taxonomy choice.

originalA.notes: Rolling, quadriliteral verbal noun. Final ة is lexical/derivational, not a required gender-agreement morpheme.

originalB.notes: Rolling, quadriliteral verbal noun; final ة has alternative lexical/feminine span treatments.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose A: lexical-whole or derivational ة for the quadriliteral verbal noun. Reject an inflectional ending solely on the basis of grammatical feminine gender.

final.notes: Rolling, quadriliteral verbal noun. Final ة is lexical/derivational, not a required gender-agreement morpheme.

originalA.notes: Tranquillity. Uses the synchronic quadriliteral root listed by the Cairo Academy, with bare hamza; historical metathesis theories are not separate accepted roots. Terminal ة may be lexical or derivational.

originalB.notes: Tranquillity. Synchronic طمءن, metathesized طءمن and the traditional triliteral lexicographic treatment طمن are retained as disputed analyses, not equally settled alternatives. Human adjudication of the root policy is needed.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose synchronic quadriliteral طمءن, matching the Academy entry for طمأنينة. Do not score historical/metathesized طءمن and traditional triliteral طمن as equivalent contemporary roots. The broader lexicographic policy still needs human confirmation.
Choose A: whole lexical noun or derivational ة; exclude productive feminine-inflection labeling for this abstract noun.

final.notes: Tranquillity. The declared synchronic convention uses طمءن, the Cairo Academy root heading. B's historical/metathesized طءمن and traditional طمن treatments remain documented in disagreements.json but are excluded from accepted roots. Final ة may stay lexical or be derivational. Low confidence flags unresolved cross-dictionary root policy, not equal acceptance of all proposed roots.

originalA.notes: Usually houses, broken plural بُيُوت. Dictionary-attested بَيُّوت also describes something kept overnight or an affair that keeps one awake.

originalB.notes: Houses/rooms, a broken plural of بيت. Internal و is part of the plural pattern.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain adjective. The Academy attests بَيُّوت for overnight-kept food and an affair that keeps someone awake; this is distinct from the common plural بُيُوت houses.

final.notes: Usually houses, broken plural بُيُوت. Dictionary-attested بَيُّوت also describes something kept overnight or an affair that keeps one awake.

originalA.notes: Knowledge عِلْم, flag/landmark عَلَم, knowing/teaching verbs with omitted vowels or shadda. Adjective additionally accepts the uncommon plural عُلْم of أعلم (cleft upper lip), explicitly listed in the dictionary.

originalB.notes: Knowledge/science (ilm), flag/landmark (alam), knew (alima), or taught/marked (allama) and related unvocalized verbal forms.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain adjective. The Academy explicitly lists عُلْم as the plural of أَعْلَم/عَلْماء for a cleft upper lip; this is a rare lexical reading, not arbitrary conversion of knowledge into an adjective.

final.notes: Knowledge عِلْم, flag/landmark عَلَم, knowing/teaching verbs with omitted vowels or shadda. Adjective additionally accepts the uncommon plural عُلْم of أعلم (cleft upper lip), explicitly listed in the dictionary.

originalA.notes: Whole-word وَعْد promise or وَعَدَ promised; Waʿd is also a conventional personal name. و + عُدْ means and return (عود); و + عُدَّ/عَدَّ/عَدّ means and count/counted/counting (عدد); و + عِدْ is and promise (وعد).

originalB.notes: Promise/promised, or the personal name Waad. Also و + عَدّ / عَدَّ (and counting / and he counted), or و + عِدْ (and promise!). Bare initial و therefore need not be a radical.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain عود: initial conjunction و plus the ordinary imperative عُدْ, return!, exactly yields وعد. The same split also supports the agreed عدد and وعد clitic readings.

final.notes: Whole-word وَعْد promise or وَعَدَ promised; Waʿd is also a conventional personal name. و + عُدْ means and return (عود); و + عُدَّ/عَدَّ/عَدّ means and count/counted/counting (عدد); و + عِدْ is and promise (وعد).

originalA.notes: قالَ said (قول) or took a midday rest (قيل). The dictionary also lists قال as a nominal word for speech and an adjective meaning speaking (قول).

originalB.notes: Said (قول), or took a midday rest (قيل). A lexical noun قال meaning speech/gossip is also attested; no generic quotation-only noun reading is assumed.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain adjective. The Academy explicitly gives a descriptive قال meaning speaking, in addition to the speech noun and the verbs. This is directly attested, not an inferred POS based on spelling.

final.notes: قالَ said (قول) or took a midday rest (قيل). The dictionary also lists قال as a nominal word for speech and an adjective meaning speaking (قول).

originalA.notes: دَعَا called/prayed has root دعو. دَعًّا pushing is an accusative verbal noun from دعع; دَعَّا can be its dual perfect. دَعَا can also be the dual imperative leave! from ودع. Dual and accusative-support alif are separately spanned in those readings.

originalB.notes: Called/supplicated (daaa, دعو), or dual imperative دَعَا (you two leave!, ودع). Final ا is stem-final in the first and a dual subject ending in the second.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain دعع: the Academy directly attests the verbal noun دَعًّا, which yields دعا when marks are omitted. Keep دعو called and ودع dual imperative leave.
Retain noun for the attested accusative verbal noun دَعًّا, alongside verb.

Choose A. A stem-final weak alif stays in stem; dual agreement or accusative-support alif uses inflectional_suffix. Subject agreement is not labeled pronominal_enclitic under this review's explicit convention.

final.notes: دَعَا called/prayed has root دعو. دَعًّا pushing is an accusative verbal noun from دعع; دَعَّا can be its dual perfect. دَعَا can also be the dual imperative leave! from ودع. Dual and accusative-support alif are separately spanned in those readings.

originalA.notes: أَكَلَ/أُكِلَ and eating/food أَكْل/أُكُل have root ءكل; أَكَلَّ made weary has root كلل. Interrogative أَ + كُلّ all is grammatical and rootless here; interrogative أَ + كَلّ dull/burdensome is lexical كلل. These parses require context.

originalB.notes: Ate/eating/food (أكل), or interrogative أ + كَلَّ (did he tire?) / كُلّ (is every/all ...?). The second root depends on a clitic reading and is less likely in isolation.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain ءكل and كلل; exclude A's null. The Academy places كُلّ, the lexical quantifier all/every, under كلل. An interrogative particle does not remove the root of its lexical host.
Retain adjective for interrogative أ + كَلّ, dull/weak, directly attested under كلل. Noun and verb are independently supported. These POS sets do not assert every root/POS pairing.

final.notes: Eating/food and ate/was eaten have root ءكل. Form IV أَكَلَّ made weary, and interrogative أ + كَلّ dull/weak or كُلّ all/every, use كلل. The Academy places the lexical quantifier under كلل; no null-root reading is accepted here. Whole-word and interrogative-particle segmentations remain. Adjective applies to كَلّ; not every root/POS/segmentation combination is a complete analysis.

originalA.notes: Imperfect plural, with active/passive and Form I/II vocalization ambiguity. The agreement prefix remains inside stem يكتب; ون is an inflectional ending. An alternative groups و and indicative ن separately.

originalB.notes: They write/are written or Form II equivalents. Imperfective ي remains in the stem because no person-prefix span type exists; ون may be bundled or split into subject و and mood ن.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose A: ون may be bundled as an inflectional suffix or split into agreement و and indicative ن, both inflectional_suffix. Reject B's subject-pronoun label under a consistent agreement-versus-object/possessor convention.

final.notes: Imperfect plural, with active/passive and Form I/II vocalization ambiguity. The agreement prefix remains inside stem يكتب; ون is an inflectional ending. An alternative groups و and indicative ن separately.

originalA.notes: Second-person feminine singular imperfect; active/passive and Form I/II readings share the letters. ين may be one ending or ي agreement plus indicative ن.

originalB.notes: You feminine singular write, or passive/derived equivalents. ين may be bundled or split into feminine subject ي and indicative ن.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose A: ين may be bundled as an inflectional suffix or split into agreement ي and indicative ن, both inflectional_suffix. Reject B's subject-pronoun label under a consistent agreement-versus-object/possessor convention.

final.notes: Second-person feminine singular imperfect; active/passive and Form I/II readings share the letters. ين may be one ending or ي agreement plus indicative ن.

originalA.notes: Plural imperative write!. Stem اكتب includes the imperative support vowel/prefix; وا combines the plural marker and its silent orthographic alif.

originalB.notes: Masculine plural imperative write!. Final وا includes the orthographic alif with the plural ending; it is not assigned a separate fictitious morpheme.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose A: وا is an inflectional subject ending, including its silent support alif. Reserve pronominal_enclitic for object/possessor complements, not subject agreement.

final.notes: Plural imperative write!. Stem اكتب includes the imperative support vowel/prefix; وا combines the plural marker and its silent orthographic alif.

originalA.notes: To/for their school or female teacher; emphatic لَ can instead precede a nominal predicate. ت is the construct form of ة. School may retain it lexically; teacher uses feminine inflection.

originalB.notes: For/to their school or female teacher; initial ل can also be emphatic la-. ة surfaces as ت before هم, with three plausible feminine boundary treatments.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain B's additional particle + lexical derivational ت segmentation: emphatic ل changes the initial clitic interpretation, not the independent school-stem derivation. Six variants are motivated by prepositional/emphatic ل and school-lexical/derivational versus teacher-feminine boundaries.

final.notes: To/for their school or female teacher; initial ل can also be emphatic in a nominal predicate. The school ending ت (construct allomorph of ة) may remain in stem or be derivational; the female-teacher ending is inflectional. These same three ending treatments are available after either prepositional or emphatic ل; هم is a possessor enclitic.

originalA.notes: And with/by their book, or their writers (كُتّاب). Intensive كَتّاب prolific writer permits adjectival use. هم is the possessive enclitic.

originalB.notes: And with/by their book; و conjunction, ب preposition, هم possessive pronoun.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain adjective provisionally for productive intensive كَتّاب, prolific in writing, alongside the established noun readings book/writers. This is an AI morphological inference; the exact intensive entry was not confirmed in the consulted Academy page. Human attestation/POS review remains open.

final.notes: And with/by their book or writers. Adjective is provisionally included for intensive كَتّاب, prolific in writing; this is a productive-pattern inference rather than a verified exact headword in the consulted Academy page. هم is the possessive enclitic. The marginal adjective alternative needs human review.

originalA.notes: Then/so at the schools; مُدارِس can also be a Form III studying/studying-with participle under the article. ف may be classified as conjunction or as a consequence/answer particle, which the contract does not distinguish.

originalB.notes: So/then in the schools; مدارس can also be a Form III participle mudaAris. ف + ب + ال are separate clitics.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain both: ف can coordinate or introduce a consequence/answer, represented as conjunction or particle. The contextless form does not determine this discourse function; all following clitic boundaries agree.

final.notes: Then/so at the schools; مُدارِس can also be a Form III studying/studying-with participle under the article. ف may be classified as conjunction or as a consequence/answer particle, which the contract does not distinguish.

originalA.notes: With/in the two cars, or two feminine traveling/mobile referents. ت is the ة allomorph before dual ين. A lexical سيارة stem can keep ت; an agreement analysis can split it or group تين.

originalB.notes: With/in the two cars. Feminine ت may stay in the oblique-dual base سيارت, be separated, or be bundled with ين; this is a segmentation-policy ambiguity.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain adjective: the Academy attests سيّار, frequently traveling, alongside lexical سيارة vehicle/car. The feminine oblique dual descriptive reading is a regular inflectional inference.

Retain all four explicitly motivated variants: lexical سيارت + ين, derivational ت in the car noun, separate feminine and dual agreement, or grouped تين. This is bounded granularity uncertainty, not interchangeable labels on every ة.

final.notes: With/in the two cars, or two feminine traveling referents. The Academy attests both lexical سيارة and descriptive سيّار. For the car noun, ت may remain in lexical سيارت or be derivational; for the descriptive reading, feminine ت and dual ين can be separate inflectional suffixes or grouped تين. Adjective/dual reading is inferred from the attested lemma.

originalA.notes: Cairo, or the feminine definite conquering/overpowering participle. The article is segmentable even in the proper name; ة may stay in the lexical stem or be feminine inflection.

originalB.notes: Cairo, or the feminine conqueror/overpowering one. ال is an article even in the established name; ة can remain in the lexical stem or be separated.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose A. Cairo keeps lexical ة inside the name stem; the feminine conquering participle can separate ة as inflectional_suffix. Name lexicalization alone does not motivate an extra derivational_suffix analysis.

final.notes: Cairo, or the feminine definite conquering/overpowering participle. The article is segmentable even in the proper name; ة may stay in the lexical stem or be feminine inflection.

originalA.notes: Two books كِتَابَان, or dual of intensive كَتَّاب prolific writer. ان is a nominative dual ending, not a numeral lexical POS.

originalB.notes: Two books: كتاب plus the nominative dual ending ان.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain adjective provisionally for the regular dual of intensive كَتّاب, prolific in writing; the ordinary noun is two books. The exact intensive entry was not confirmed in the consulted Academy page, so this marginal inference needs human attestation/POS review.

final.notes: Two books, with nominative dual ان. Adjective is provisionally included for the dual of intensive كَتّاب, prolific in writing, a productive-pattern inference rather than an exact verified inflected dictionary form. This marginal alternative needs human review; dual number does not make lexical POS numeral.

originalA.notes: Usually demonstrative هٰذا, treated as one stem or attention particle ه + demonstrative ذا. Unvocalized هذًّا is an accusative verbal noun rapid recitation/cutting from هذذ; هذَّا can be a dual perfect. The rare noun is attested in Lisan al-Arab; the dual is inferred.

originalB.notes: Demonstrative this, either lexical whole or attention ه + ذا. Also هَذَّا, dual perfective/imperative of هذّ (cut/recite quickly); the dual reading is an inflectional inference from the cited classical verb.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain noun: Lisan al-Arab directly records the accusative verbal noun هذا for rapid reading/cutting (هذًّا without marks). Keep demonstrative and inferred dual verbal readings.

Choose A. Keep the demonstrative whole or split attention ه from ذا. For the lexical noun/dual verb, terminal alif can be inflectional; exclude B's pronominal_enclitic subject label. Attention-particle surface allocation remains convention-sensitive.

final.notes: Usually demonstrative هٰذا, whole or attention ه + ذا. Lisan al-Arab directly attests هذًّا rapid recitation/cutting, yielding هذا without marks; هذّا as a dual verb is inferred. The lexical final alif is inflectional (accusative support/dual agreement), not a possessor/object pronoun. Demonstrative attention-particle segmentation remains a low-confidence surface convention.

originalA.notes: Independent first-person plural pronoun; no lexical Arabic root assigned.

originalB.notes: We (naHnu), or we yearn/long (naHinnu) from حنّ. In the verbal reading the imperfective ن remains inside the stem.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Choose B: root حنن is required by the ordinary imperfective نَحِنّ, we yearn, formed from the Academy-attested حنّ. Retain null for independent pronoun نحن.
Choose B: the same unvocalized letters support both pronoun and verb. Imperfective person ن remains inside stem because there is no inflectional_prefix category.

final.notes: Independent pronoun we has null root. Unvocalized نَحِنّ, we yearn/long, is a regular imperfective of حنّ with root حنن. The verbal form is inferred from the attested lemma; its person prefix ن remains inside the single stem.

originalA.notes: Usually independent I. Also contracted أَنَّا that we (particle plus fused pronoun), or أَنًّا groaning / أَنَّا they two groaned from أنّ. Whole-stem segmentation is retained for the contracted grammatical token because the schema has no shared/fused span; separate ا represents accusative support or dual ending for lexical readings. Contraction segmentation remains uncertain.

originalB.notes: I (anaa); or أَنَّا, dual of أنّ (groaned), and أَنًّا, accusative groaning verbal noun, when marks are omitted. The rare alternatives require context; final ا is dual agreement or orthographic accusative support.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain particle for contracted أَنّا, that we, alongside pronoun I and the attested groaning noun/inferred dual verb. The particle + نا contraction is an AI grammatical inference and remains low confidence in this surface-only scheme.

Choose A. Keep fused grammatical أَنّا as one stem because shared ن cannot be represented uniquely by nonoverlapping spans; final ا alone is not the pronoun نا. In lexical noun/dual-verb readings the alif is inflectional, not pronominal_enclitic.

final.notes: Usually independent I. Contracted أَنّا, that we, is treated as particle-headed and rootless, with the fused token kept whole; there is no unique nonoverlapping allocation of shared ن to أن and نا. Groaning أَنًّا is dictionary-attested; the dual verb أَنّا is inferred from أنّ (root ءنن). Final alif may be an inflectional span for these lexical readings. A final-alif-only pronoun span is excluded. The grammatical contraction convention remains unresolved.

originalA.notes: مِنْ from is preposition; مَنْ who/whoever is pronoun, both rootless. مَنّ favor/manna or مَنَّ bestowed has root منن. Rare imperative مِنْ lie! (مين) and مُنْ provide for! (مون) follow the attested hollow verbs مان; those forms are inferred rather than directly cited.

originalB.notes: From (min), who/whoever (man), manna/favour/counting-a-favour noun (mann), or granted a favour/reproached (manna) and related geminate verbal readings. Function readings have null root.

fieldDecisions.rationale: Retain مين and مون. The Academy attests مان with imperfective i for lying and u for provisioning. Regular hollow imperatives yield مِنْ and مُنْ, both the frozen unvocalized من. These are conjugational inferences, not exact imperative quotations.

final.notes: مِنْ from is preposition; مَنْ who/whoever is pronoun, both rootless. مَنّ favor/manna or مَنَّ bestowed has root منن. Rare imperative مِنْ lie! (مين) and مُنْ provide for! (مون) follow the attested hollow verbs مان; those forms are inferred rather than directly cited.

unresolvedCases.issue: Synchronic طمءن is selected; historical/triliteral lexicographic alternatives are excluded pending human agreement on root policy.
Fused ي can represent base/case/pronoun material. The accepted boundary is an explicit allocation convention, not unique morpheme recovery.
The demonstrative may be lexical whole or attention ه + ذا; a human segmentation policy is needed.
Particle-headed contracted أَنّا is included, but shared ن prevents a unique nonoverlapping particle/pronoun segmentation.
Intensive adjective كَتّاب is retained by productive morphological inference; exact lemma/POS attestation remains to be independently confirmed.
Dual intensive adjective is retained by productive morphological inference; exact lemma/POS attestation remains to be independently confirmed.
